chunks: From him, from his fathers, peace be upon them.
That the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) saw a man throwing stones in the mosque, so he said, "It kept cursing until it fell."
Then he said, "Throwing stones in the gathering place is from the character of the people of Lot."
"And you commit in your gathering the evil."
He said, "It is the throwing of stones."
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of throwing stones in the mosque according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration in the chapter on the virtue of mosques, highlighting the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) unique attribution of 'cursing' (la'nah) to the stone itself as it traversed the sacred space, thereby elevating the spiritual status of the mosque. By linking the act of *khaadhf* (throwing stones) to the people of Lot, the tradition underscores the continuity of moral decay in communal spaces, while the explicit identification of the Quranic 'nadī' as this specific act provides a concrete jurisprudential application of the verse.
